From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Thanks Alex — great to meet the team. Per your asks, below is a prioritized 3-engine shortlist and immediate artifacts to help your evaluation. I kept the rationale tight so you can pass to procurement/infra quickly.

Shortlist (prioritized):
1) Redwood-XL-8B (int4 quantized) — Why: best balance for your throughput profile (avg. 1.2s per 512-token response on T4-like instances), strong end-to-end quality on support summarization in our benchmarks, and the lowest per-token cost after quantization. Tradeoffs: less headroom for long-context hallucination cases; consider increased temperature tuning for creative summaries.
2) Llama-3-7B-Instruct (int8/float16 mix) — Why: lower latency (0.8s/512 tokens) on smaller instances, robust for short summarization and routing classification. Tradeoffs: slightly lower factuality on long multipart tickets in our regression sets; cheaper infra at small scale.
3) OpenR-13B-4Q (13B, 4-bit quant) — Why: highest raw quality on complex multi-turn summaries; good for cases where precision matters. Tradeoffs: ~2x cost vs Redwood-XL-8B and higher inference latency (1.8–2.4s depending on sequence length).

Benchmarks and artifacts attached/linked:
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BenchmarkSheet (tab: BrightWave-demo)
- Prompt sets we used: prompt_sets_v1.zip (contains 12 labeled prompts + expected-answer rubric)
- CSV export of raw perf numbers: benchmarks_v2.csv (attachment)

Quality regression notes (short):
- Regression surface: multi-turn consistency and entity preservation across long ticket threads.
- Mitigations we recommend: holdback prompt sets, continuous regression evaluation on your live traffic sample (1% mirrored), and a minimum A/B rollout with automatic rollback on NPS/factuality drop.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick sync (30m) Thursday to confirm which of the 3 you want in the POC and procurement signals we should expect.
- We can provision a 2-week pilot with Redwood-XL-8B int4 and the Llama-3-7B variant; include test harness and eval harness for your team.

Attaching the CSV and prompt_pack. If you want, I can also spin up a short regression job and share the seed outputs for your top 20 tickets.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(attachment: benchmarks_v2.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-22T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finalist engines — quantization path & mitigation playbook

Looping in a couple quick operational concerns and an internal ask before we send anything formal to procurement.

Operational points: 
- Regression detection: we should propose a concrete regression suite for BrightWave — recommend 4 buckets (factuality, entity preservation, hallucination on long tickets, routing accuracy). We should include threshold-based alerts and a daily regression digest for their CS team.
- Quantization caveat: for Redwood-XL-8B int4, there are edge cases where OOV tokenization on domain-specific entities (product codes) degrades precision. We can mitigate with a domain token patch (adds ~0.3% memory) and small fine-tune; note this in the SOW.
- Canary rollout: recommend traffic ramp 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers on regression metrics.

Deliverables I think we need before procurement: 
1) A short SOW paragraph (1/2 page) calling out quantization path + mitigations.
2) Regression gating thresholds (CSV) and a quick A/B plan.
3) Pricing sensitivity note for Redwood-XL-8B vs OpenR-13B under 100M tokens/month usage.

Attaching the CSV of the latest perf numbers and the prompt pack we used (zipped). I'll draft the SOW paragraph and send by EOD.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Product Lead, Inference Economics, Redwood Inference
